CLINK.justification: the body, status code, and content length are chained into one response

ENGAGR.justification: the target is held as both a mutable user file and an immutable raw byte source while the reader starts

EVALF.justification: these states refute the read path by producing an error body without raw bytes

EVALT.justification: these states affirm that the descriptor is readable and the buffer holds the file bytes

FFUSE.justification: the read arms rejoin into one body and the open arms rejoin into one envelope

FSPLIT.justification: the reader forks on whether the file opens and, after opening, whether the read completes

IFIX.justification: the read bytes are fixed as the response payload and cannot be rewritten by later steps

IMSCRIB.justification: the response identifies itself as the output of this reader without changing the payload

TANCH.justification: the final envelope contains the status, headers, and body and closes the reader's work
